title: Public Wi-Fi: what's real and what's myth
description: Is public Wi-Fi really dangerous? HTTPS changed the picture. Here's what still matters and what's outdated advice.

scenes.say: Everyone says never use public Wi-Fi. That advice is mostly out of date.

left.label: Myth
items: Every cafe network is a trap

scenes.say: Most sites use HTTPS, so someone on the same network can't read your logins or messages. The real risks are different, and a bit sneakier.
A fake hotspot copies a real network's name. Join it, and an attacker sits in the middle, and can try to send you to fake login pages. Two networks with the same name should make you pause.

steps: Ask staff for the exact name
scenes.say: So confirm the network name, keep your phone updated, and never click past browser warnings. For everyday browsing, HTTPS and updates do most of the work.

scenes.sub: if you join the right network
scenes.say: So, mostly fine, if you join the right network. Follow for more myth busting.
